# Coverage of the FastAPI, Pydantic and SQLAlchemy documentation

<!-- Generated by corpus/coverage.py from a corpus/run.py run: do not edit by hand. -->

py2axum is measured on the examples of the official documentation: every app of FastAPI's `docs_src/` (FastAPI 0.142.3), replayed with FastAPI's own tests (`tests/test_tutorial/`) against the Python reference and against the binary, and every Pydantic 2.14.0 documentation block that validates a model, served by a minimal FastAPI route around each model. Responses are compared as the [conformance harness](advanced/conformance.md) compares them: status, headers, body byte for byte, key order included. The SQLAlchemy documentation has [its own section](#sqlalchemy). The bench is in `corpus/` ([how it works](https://github.com/larrymotalavigne/py2axum/blob/main/corpus/README.md)).

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| identical | every compared response is the same |
| documented | the responses differ only by a [documented difference](supported.md) (the order of a `set`, an integer beyond 64 bits) |
| differs | at least one response differs (a bug, unless listed in [supported.md](supported.md)) |
| refused | py2axum refuses the example at translation, with the reason at file:line |
| error | the translator crashed, or the generated code did not compile or start |
| untested | translated, but no official test sends it a request |
| docs-only | its tests only request `/openapi.json` or `/docs`, which the binary does not serve |
| nondeterministic | Python's own responses vary from run to run (`random`): compared, never counted |
| reference-fails | the Python reference itself fails (SQLAlchemy section only): listed, never counted |

The OpenAPI schema and documentation pages are not served by the binary (see [supported.md](supported.md#not-supported)): those requests are sent to both servers but not compared. Requests a test sends while it sets `app.dependency_overrides` are not compared either (only the in-process app sees the override). A JWT in a body is compared claim by claim, its `exp`/`iat`/`nbf` within 2 seconds (the two servers are called one after the other). The share is that of the `identical` and `documented` examples among those a test exercises over HTTP (`untested`, `docs-only` and `nondeterministic` ones are counted apart).

## Summary

| Corpus | Examples | identical | documented | differs | refused | error | untested | docs-only | nondeterministic | reference-fails | Share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FastAPI | 339 | 284 | 5 | 0 | 35 | 0 | 11 | 4 | 0 | 0 | **90.6 %** |
| Pydantic | 238 | 213 | 3 | 0 | 22 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | **90.8 %** |

Bench run: discover 9.8 s, check 93.4 s, generate 543.6 s, build 740.4 s, replay 558.0 s, total 1945.2 s.

<!-- sqlalchemy:start -->
## SQLAlchemy

The SQLAlchemy 2.1.4 documentation is run as SQLAlchemy runs it, as doctests (the units of `test/base/test_tutorials.py`: the Unified Tutorial, the ORM Quick Start, the ORM Querying Guide, large collections, asyncio; then other ORM, extension and Core pages, as written). Each code block that executes SQL is an example: a minimal FastAPI route runs it, preceded by the earlier statements of the page it depends on, in a session of its own, and returns what the block prints and displays. A block that only shows a `SELECT` for its SQL text is executed too (rows returned). Each route exists twice: `sync` (a `Session` dependency) and `async` (an `AsyncSession` with `expire_on_commit=False`, `await` on its methods). PostgreSQL, the database put back to the page's seed data before every request; the Python reference and the binary are compared as above. `reference-fails`: the Python reference fails on the route (mostly a lazy load under `AsyncSession`, which raises `MissingGreenlet`).

The examples are in three scopes. **ORM**: queries a route runs with the ORM (select, joins, aggregates, CTE, subqueries, insert/update/delete, relationships, loader options, types, extensions); its share is the one py2axum 1.0 requires (90 %). **Core**: the Core chapters of the Unified Tutorial (`Table`, `text()`). **Outside API use**: a block about DDL, reflection, events or the pool, or about a session's state across statements (identity map, `expunge`, pending sets), the way a script or a long-lived session works. Core and outside are measured and published, without a threshold.

| Scope / variant | Examples | identical | documented | differs | refused | error | untested | docs-only | nondeterministic | reference-fails | Share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **SQLAlchemy ORM** (1.0 threshold: 90 %) | 276 | 243 | 0 | 0 | 16 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 15 | **93.8 %** |
| SQLAlchemy Core (aimed at for 1.1) | 126 | 110 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0 | **88.7 %** |
| outside API use (measured only) | 78 | 32 | 0 | 0 | 44 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | **42.1 %** |
| sync | 239 | 201 | 0 | 0 | 36 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0 | **84.8 %** |
| async | 241 | 184 | 0 | 0 | 38 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 17 | **82.9 %** |
| all of SQLAlchemy | 480 | 385 | 0 | 0 | 74 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 | 17 | **83.9 %** |

Not in the corpus: 22 examples (both variants) the bench cannot run as written: Python fails on PostgreSQL (22) (SQLite-only SQL, a statement of the page that fails before them).
